what:
J2 measurement (docs/plans/ai_judge.md, "LLM call boundary and cost"): does the existing model rules review flag the
plain version's sawmill rule, which charges the price once rather than per log? One paid call on the review model.

Input: the sawmill world as built (evidence/declared-laws/s2-pencil-2/run-log.jsonl line 1) with the plain version's
accepted rule added (evidence/ai-judge/plain-baseline/pencil-sawmill-buys-logs.json). Output: review.json beside this.

findings.description_words: Specialist businesses continually make, move, and sell pencils through a recurring supply chain.
findings.problem: Sawing logs into slats reduces the world's total of the cedar resource (which counts standing cedar and business logs), but the cedar-total law only allows cut-cedar to change that total, so saw-slats will always be refused by the law. In addition, saw-slats takes logs directly from the logger for free instead of sawing the logs the sawmill bought with buy-cedar-logs.

findings.description_words: Specialist businesses continually make, move, and sell pencils through a recurring supply chain.
findings.problem: The first effect of deliver-pencil-shipment subtracts the carrier's shipment cargo from itself, reducing it to zero before the second effect adds the carrier's shipment cargo to the shop's packed_pencils. This either transfers zero pencils to the shop and destroys the cargo (which the pencils-total law also refuses) or relies on reading the already-zeroed field.

findings.description_words: Specialist businesses continually make, move, and sell pencils through a recurring supply chain.
findings.problem: The customer starts with waiting_for_pencils set to 1 and buy-pencil reduces it by 1 on each purchase, but customer-demand-arrives only increases the shop's waiting_customers count and never increments the co-located customer's waiting_for_pencils count. After a single purchase, no further pencils can ever be sold.
